answers.falsifier: a record written read-only through the door is removed through the door: the file is gone and a remove entry is journaled ; a writable record still removes as before, and the door still writes seals read-only
answers.how: In remove() in cairn/tools/artifact/artifact.py, after the jurisdiction check and the journal entry is built, os.chmod(p, stat.S_IWRITE | stat.S_IREAD) when the file is not writable, then unlink. The store's mode for new seals is untouched. Proof in scratch roots: write a record with mode 0o444 through the door, remove it through the door, assert the file is gone and a remove entry with sha_after absent was journaled, and that a writable record still removes.
answers.title: the artifact door's remove clears the read-only bit before it unlinks, so a sealed validation can be removed on Windows
answers.traces_to: Law 7: a door that cannot do its one job on a platform fails loudly but leaves the record stuck; Law 4: removal goes through the door, so the door must work where it runs.
answers.what: artifact.remove clears the read-only bit before it unlinks, so a read-only record such as a sealed validation is removed through the door on Windows as on Linux, journaled with sha_after absent.
